name: Janūbi Arabic (southern Saudi)

ancestors.notes: Inherited placeholder table; see notes on ar-SA-x-janubi.

notes: Southern Saudi Arabia, the label used in the SADA corpus. ATTESTED AS A LABEL, NOT AS A LANGUOID. No source describes a 'Janūbi' variety as a unit: the literature describes named villages of ʿAsīr and the Tihāma that disagree with each other at village-to-village distance, and the region's described varieties already have their own specs (ar-SA-x-rijal-alma, ar-SA-x-tihama-qahtan). The parent is the peninsular proto-node rather than either of those, because choosing one would assert a grouping no source supports. The entry exists so the corpus label resolves; it is not a claim that the variety is uniform.
